title: leucanthemopsis pallida subsp. pseudopulverulenta
intro: Leucanthemopsis pallida subsp. pseudopulverulenta, commonly known as alpine daisy, is a species of flowering plant in the aster family, characterized by its small white or pink flowers and hairy leaves. The alpine daisy has been used in traditional medicine to promote digestive health and alleviate symptoms of gastrointestinal disorders due to its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Leucanthemopsis pallida subsp. pseudopulverulenta may include soothing digestive issues, reducing inflammation, and exhibiting antioxidant activity, although more research is needed to confirm these effects. The bioactive constituents of this plant are primarily flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which contribute to its potential medicinal properties.
